To ensure we are on the same page, here is a summary of the case:
We understand that when moving between “G” deck to “B” deck, the connection is unstable, and WiFi access points appear to be in normal status.
At this stage, the issue is not related to Xchange, since if so, all crews at all decks will be affected. Next, please advise:
1 Do you encounter such issue when you remain on both decks, without movement? If the issue is due to a particular WiFi hot spot, then the error shall appear even if you stay on the same deck

2 When you got the 'failed to connect to Xchange" error, please check the WiFi signal on your mobile device. If you lose the connection around the same spot, then it can be a local WiFi coverage issue onboard
If you have a laptop available, we can test a bit further than item 2:
- Connect the laptop to Xchange WiFi, you don't have to login.
- Press windows Start button. Type "cmd" in the search bar, and click on cmd.exe in the search result. A black window shall pop up
- Type command "ping 10.0.2.1 -t", then press Enter. Screenshot attached below for your reference.
If you get "Reply from 10.0.2.1: bytes 32 xxx ms" in the black window. That means you should be able to connect to Xchange home page.
If the result is "Request time out" like below, that means Xchange is not reachable, and you most likely will get the "failed to connect" error.
So you can bring the laptop and move between the decks, to monitor when you get the "request timed out", to tell exactly when you lose the access to Xchange.

ACU passed all diagnostic tests previously. Dash "-" means a particular test was not required and skipped.
Per the tracert test, there is another device between the PC and Xchange LAN 1. Let's try direct connection.
Connect a PC directly to Xchange LAN 2, and then configure its IP as DHCP per below:
1)On the PC, Click the Start button (in left down corner of the screen), and then click on Control Panel.
2)In the search box, type Network and Sharing Center, select Network and Sharing Center from search results, then click on Change adapter settings
3)Right-click the connection we need to change, most frequently called "Local Area Connection" or "Ethernet", and then click Properties.
4)Click the Networking tab. Under This connection uses the following items, is a list of options. Click on Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and then click Properties.
5) Check "Obtain an IP address automatically" and Obtain DNS server address automatically"
6)Click OK button and next Close button.
Then open web browser, and test if you can reach Xchange at http://10.0.2.1 or https://10.0.2.1.
If the above works, and you can activate IOP in Xchange, then we can remotely troubleshoot VSAT.
If it still doesn't work, please follow the below procedure to download the ACU log.
Below On the front panel of Antenna Control Unit, there are 2 USB ports, hidden under plastic cover on the left side.
1. Connect USB flash drive to USB port DN on the Antenna Control Unit.
2. If screen does not automatically go to [USB FUNCTION] menu, keep pressing right arrow button until you reach that menu.
3. In [USB FUNCTION] press up or down arrow button to select COPY LOG DATA.
4. Press OK button to start copying.
5. Copy progress in percentages will be shown on the display.
6. Once it is finished remove the USB flash drive.
7. Antenna logs will be stored in folder Intellian/Logs/
File name of the logs has following structure X_YYYYMMDD_hhmmss
X - type of log, this can have following values: G, M, O, S, R and T
R and T logs do not follow this name structure.
Please zip the files for last 1 week (based on the timestamp in file name) and send it to us.

In normal circumstance, if Captain logins his Master account from a non-machine PC, then he shall see a green "Connect" button on the top of page, to establish internet access. And then, data from his PC will follow the rules as defined for "Captain" group.

However, if he logins on a Machine computer, then he will not see such button, but only a message saying "Session already started". That means data from the PC will still follow the defined rules for "Machine" group, going through the "firewall" and etc, as you mentioned.
Thus, using Master account on a Machine PC will not change its device priority (Sealink v.s. Starlink) or firewall rules.

If possible, Captain can use a his Master account on a non-machine PC to use Starlink for DigiDoc app. Or,if such app has to run on a machine PC, we can link you with your Marlink Service Manager and technical team, to review the fleet IT design. I'm sure they can find a solution to this.

If above is not possible, please follow procedure to download the ACU log.
Below On the front panel of Antenna Control Unit, there are 2 USB ports, hidden under plastic cover on the left side.
1. Connect USB flash drive to USB port DN on the Antenna Control Unit.
2. If screen does not automatically go to [USB FUNCTION] menu, keep pressing right arrow button until you reach that menu.
3. In [USB FUNCTION] press up or down arrow button to select COPY LOG DATA.
4. Press OK button to start copying.
5. Copy progress in percentages will be shown on the display.
6. Once it is finished remove the USB flash drive.
7. Antenna logs will be stored in folder Intellian/Logs/
File name of the logs has following structure X_YYYYMMDD_hhmmss
X - type of log, this can have following values: G, M, O, S, R and T
R and T logs do not follow this name structure.
Please zip the files for last 1 week (based on the timestamp in file name) and send it to us.

There are a few factors that contribute to discrepancy.
First of all, Xchange traffic log use GiB, while P360 displays Starlink quota in GB. For example, 314 GiB in Xchange log is equal to 337GB.
Secondly, Starlink has background traffic for the antenna and GPS management, which is not included in XChange log, as such traffic does not pass through Xchange.
Finally, such discrepancy is also due to the packet retransmission over the satellite link, since such traffic is not counted in XChange log, but in Starlink log.

column1: • Subject: Marlink Ticket [1751162] - APL Le Havre - Starlink ref:RE: [Portal360] Starlink Quota Reached: APL Le Havre
The numbers displayed in Xchange and backend system are not exactly the same, and there are a few factors that contribute to discrepancy:
First of all, Xchange traffic log use GiB, while backend uses displays quota in GB, and 1GiB=1.074 GB, so that is about 7% difference.
Secondly, Starlink has background traffic for the antenna and GPS management, which is not included in XChange log, as such traffic does not pass through Xchange.
Finally, such discrepancy is also due to the packet retransmission over the satellite link, since such traffic is not counted in XChange log, but in Starlink log.

You can check the starlink data consumption per screenshot below.
The numbers displayed in Xchange and backend system are not exactly the same, and there are a few factors that contribute to discrepancy:
First of all, Xchange traffic log use GiB, while backend uses displays quota in GB, and 1GiB=1.074 GB, so that is about 7% difference.
Secondly, Starlink has background traffic for the antenna and GPS management, which is not included in XChange log, as such traffic does not pass through Xchange.
Finally, such discrepancy is also due to the packet retransmission over the satellite link, since such traffic is not counted in XChange log, but in Starlink log.

That is a good question, and I'll try my best to explain this.
Starlink uses a "cell" concept in their system, which is very similar to our GSM mobile network. Basically, cell is the smallest coverage unit, which starlink applies restriction rules on.
Please refer to below screenshots, your cell number: 85823013fffffff; GH Challenger cell number: 858230b3fffffff.

So from Starlink point of view, your good vessel and GH Challenger are under the coverage of different cells. In this case, your vessel is considered under Angola water, while GH Challenger is not. Thus, Starlink may apply different restriction rules. This is solely controlled by Starlink, and we can't change it.
Hopefully this clarifies your doubt, and please feel free to contact us shall you have further questions.

>> First consume 1,000 MB on VSAT (Sealink)
>> Then, switch to 1,000 MB on Starlink once VSAT data is exhausted

As per our communication with Laurel Office, the vessel crew should receive a total of 1 GB/day across both VSAT and Starlink. This would ensure that vessels in non-Starlink zones can seamlessly use VSAT without facing restrictions.

column4: You can review the ticket by going to:

column1: • Subject: Marlink Ticket [1725526] - Laurel Ship Management Pte Ltd ref:(#5751846) Inquiry About Data Allocation Across Laurel Fleet
- "when Starlink is un﻿available, will the crew be able to fully utilize 1,000 MB of data on VSAT (Sealink). "
Marlink: Yes. If Starlink is not available, then Xchange will switch to Sealink, and crew shall be able to consume all the $10 allowance on Sealink, which is equivalent to 1000MB.
- "If we change the channel preference, setting Sealink as priority 1 and Starlink as priority 2 (refer to screenshot no. 2), will the crew be able to:
>> Then, switch to 1,000 MB on Starlink once VSAT data is exhausted"

Marlink: No. There are two reasons: firstly, after a crew consumes 1000 MB on VSAT, he will have depleted all $10, and have no allowance left; secondly, as long as VSAT is online, crew doesn't have the option to choose to switch to Starlink. Thus, even if he still has allowance left, he can only continue to surf on VSAT but not on Starlink.

To meet your requirement that " crew should receive a total of 1 GB/day across both VSAT and Starlink", you may consider issue each crew two accounts, one for Starlink and one for Sealink. Then crew can choose which one to use at his convenience.

column13: Dear Valued Customer

We are writing to inform you of an important update to the authentication method for accessing the Data Manager application. Starting 15th February, all users will need to log in via a Portal360 account, utilising a two-factor authentication (2FA) process. This change is part of our commitment to enhancing security and ensuring compliance with industry best practices.
The login to the Data Manager will then require a two-step process:
1.    MFA Authentication page:
Select “Sign in with Portal360”
Confirm the login using the second factor authentication (e.g. using Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or similar)
2.    You will be redirected to the regular Data Manager page where you can log in with the current Data Manager account/passwords.

3.    For the first step, we kindly request you to send us the list of users from your company (email addresses) who need to access the Data Manager application to servicedesk@marlink.com. We will verify if Portal360 accounts exist for these email addresses and if not, create them in advance.

At Marlink, we are committed to providing secure and seamless solutions that enable your business to operate efficiently and with confidence. The transition to Portal360 with two-factor authentication is a key step in strengthening the security of your applications and data.
Should you have any questions or require assistance, our Service Desk team is here to help. Please don’t hesitate to reach out via servicedesk@marlink.com.
We appreciate your cooperation and look forward to supporting you throughout this process.
The Marlink Team
